subject: Question: how tokens are billed across Chat / Responses / legacy endpoints
messages:
From: Andrew Li <andrew@neostore.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>; procurement@neostore.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice question: Feb hosted usage - token mismatch

Hi Mina,

We just received our January invoice and there are a few lines that look off. The invoice shows ~1.2M tokens billed under "responses" while our engineering team believes all calls were routed through the Chat Completions endpoint (we use the SDK integration). That difference is materially affecting our spend for Q1 and procurement is asking for a quick reconciliation.

I've attached the invoice PDF and highlighted the lines in question (neostore-invoice-202601.pdf). Can you help explain how tokens are accounted for between: Chat Completions, the new Responses API, and our legacy completions calls? Specifically:
- Do the three endpoints count request / prompt tokens the same way?
- Are there any automatic migrations / routing that might have caused some calls to be billed as Responses instead of Chat?
- Can you provide a simple example calculation (request tokens + response tokens => billed units) so our finance team can follow?

We'd appreciate a prompt answer — our renewal lead wants to understand before the end of the month.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Li
Director of Product
Neostore

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Invoice question: Feb hosted usage - token mismatch

Hi Andrew — thanks for the note and the invoice. I pulled your account usage and started a quick mapping; below is a concise explanation and next steps.

Quick answer (tl;dr): the three endpoints can show different billed lines because they account for tokens slightly differently and because routing/versioning can cause a request to be recorded against a different meter. We should be able to map the disputed lines to request_ids.

How the endpoints differ (high level):
- Chat Completions (chat/completions): billed as "chat_tokens" (count includes message role markers and any conversation history passed in the request).
- Responses (responses API): billed as "response_tokens" — this counts the full generated output plus the prompt payload when using some features (tool-calls or structured output can change what is counted).
- Legacy completions (v1/completions): billed under "completions_tokens"; older SDKs sometimes send longer serialized prompts which can inflate request token counts.

Common causes for mismatch:
1) SDK versions: older SDKs fallback to legacy endpoints for certain model names; that would show up as completions tokens even though your code called the high-level chat client.
2) Proxying/routing: if a request used a model alias that is backed by a Responses-compatible runtime, usage can appear under Responses.
3) Context size: if you pass long conversation history (many system + user messages) the request-token portion becomes a larger share of the billed tokens.

Example calc (simple):
- Request payload: 450 tokens (conversation + system)
- Generated response: 150 tokens
- Billed tokens = request (450) + generation (150) = 600 tokens billed (then converted per 1k tokens unit in invoice).

What I need from you to reconcile the invoice:
- A few sample request_ids or timestamps for calls you believe were Chat Completions but were billed under Responses/completions.
- Any SDK version you were using in January (we commonly see 0.9.x clients that hit legacy paths).

Attached: our current ratecard (redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf) — it includes the unit definitions and per-1k token prices for all hosted endpoints. I can also attach a CSV of the raw call logs for the date ranges once you confirm which days to inspect.

Next steps:
1) If you share 3–5 sample request_ids/timestamps we will map them and send a line-by-line reconcile.
2) If we identify a mis-routing or billing error on our side we'll propose a billing adjustment / courtesy credit.
3) If this is a behavior change (e.g., long context + new SDK), we'll recommend an SDK update + a short guidance doc to keep token usage predictable.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Friday to walk through the mapping?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>

Hi Andrew — thanks again for sending the invoice. I dug into your account usage for Jan and attached a small CSV of the call logs (sample-call-logs.csv) that map request_id -> endpoint -> request_tokens -> response_tokens -> billed_tokens. Below is a short reconciliation and a proposed resolution.

Summary of findings:
- 78% of the billed tokens that appeared under "responses" came from calls that were routed to the legacy completions path due to an SDK version mismatch (our backend logs show the agent string from 0.9.3).
- The remaining 22% were legitimate Responses API calls (you were experimenting with the "structured_output" flag on Jan 10, which increases counted prompt size).

Illustrative calculation (from sample-call-logs.csv):
- call id: r-20260110-009
- endpoint: v1/completions (legacy)
- request tokens: 520
- response tokens: 180
- billed tokens: 700 -> invoice shows the line under "responses/completions" depending on the meter mapping

What this means: the usage is valid but mis-categorized in your expectation — those legacy calls count the full serialized prompt and can look larger than a modern chat payload. There is no double-billing.

Proposed remediation:
1) Courtesy credit: Redwood will issue a $2,000 credit against the January invoice while we complete a full line-by-line map. If we find any confirmed overbilling due to our routing layer, we'll issue an additional adjustment.
2) Action item for Neostore eng: upgrade SDK to 1.4.x (we've included an SDK compatibility note in the attached ratecard).
3) 30-minute walkthrough: I'll schedule a time next week to go through the sample logs and show how to interpret tokens and meter names.

If that sounds reasonable I'll route the credit request to billing (cc Marissa) and we can get you an updated invoice within 3–5 business days. Also attaching the ratecard again for reference.

Thanks — would you like the walkthrough on Tuesday or Wednesday next week?

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
